Clip triangles by a rectangle

Source: R/tri_ops.R
tri_clip_rect.Rd

Keep the parts of the triangles inside a rectangle, as triangles again: ST_ClipByBox2D() that returns a mesh.

Usage

tri_clip_rect(x, rect)

Arguments

x

A wkpool_tri.

rect

The rectangle: a wk::rct() or c(xmin, ymin, xmax, ymax).

Value

A wkpool_tri with the input vertices plus the new ones (origin column "clip" for new vertices when the pool has an origin column; use pool_compact() to drop unused vertices), keeping the feature and part of each source triangle. The source triangle row of each output triangle is in attribute "source".

Details

Triangles inside the rectangle are kept as they are, triangles outside are dropped, and each triangle that crosses a side is cut to a convex polygon and fanned back into triangles. New vertices where edges cross the sides are added to the vertex pool, and a point where a shared edge crosses a side is computed the same way from both of its triangles, so neighbouring pieces share it exactly. Slivers of zero area on a side are dropped.

Examples

v <- data.frame(.vx = 1:6, x = c(0, 1, 1, 0, 2, 2), y = c(0, 0, 1, 1, 0, 1))
tri <- new_wkpool_tri(v, vx0 = c(1, 1, 2, 2), vx1 = c(2, 3, 5, 6),
                      vx2 = c(3, 4, 6, 3), feature = c(1, 1, 2, 2))
clipped <- tri_clip_rect(tri, c(0.5, 0.25, 1.5, 0.75))
tri_measures(clipped)
#>   group area perimeter centroid_x centroid_y point_x   point_y xmin ymin xmax
#> 1     1 0.25         2       0.75        0.5    0.75 0.5000000  0.5 0.25  1.0
#> 2     2 0.25         2       1.25        0.5    1.25 0.5833333  1.0 0.25  1.5
#>   ymax
#> 1 0.75
#> 2 0.75
